# SAM 3D Body: motion from footage

Recovers a **3D body animation** from a video and exports it as a **skeletal GLB**, plus a render preview of the
same motion. The clip *is* the motion source - there is no rigging or retargeting here, and the skin is Meta's
MHR, so putting this motion on *your* character is the engine's retarget step.

**The two settings that matter - the upstream template gets both wrong** (E6/E8):

* `SAM3DBody_Smooth.rotation_threshold_degrees` = **0** (upstream ships 15). This knob *disables* smoothing
  above a given root rotation rate "to preserve fast spins", and at 15 - below the schema's own default of 30 -
  it switches smoothing off exactly when the motion gets fast.
* `BuildPoseFile.format.bone_smooth_window` = **9** (upstream ships 0 = off). The export stage has its own
  smoother, and its tooltip says it exists to calm "spins/jitter where upstream Smooth misses spikes".

Measured on a fast dance clip, going from the upstream defaults to these: single-frame pops **8 -> 2**, worst
pop **174 -> 60 deg**, motion bandwidth **3.36 -> 0.68 Hz**. Bigger is not better - the one residual spike
*grows* with the window (57.7 / 92.5 / 126.3 deg at 9 / 15 / 21), so 9 is the sweet spot.

**Length:** `Video Slice` decides how much footage is processed - it ships at 5 s. Measured at 720x1280 (E15): 121 frames 111 s / 19.6 GB, 242 frames 210 s / 22.1 GB, **290 frames (12 s) completes at 21.6 GB, and 363 frames (15 s) OOMs** - so ~12 s is the practical ceiling there, and roughly 2.2x that frame count at 480x848, since memory follows pixels. Time is linear (~0.9 s/frame), so it is the slice that runs out, not patience; the failure is a hard CUDA OOM mid-run. Beyond it, process the clip in slices.

**Resolution: the flow caps the input at 480x848, and that buys length.** The artefact is a skeleton, and pixels-per-person is what matters rather than the frame's nominal size - measured, processing the same clip at 480x848 instead of 720x1280 changes the recovered joints by a **mean of 1.5 deg** (worst 4.4 deg, the wrists) and is visually indistinguishable (E16). Since per-frame memory follows pixels, the cap roughly doubles how much footage fits: ~12 s uncapped becomes ~**27 s** capped. It is an `ImageResizeKJ` with `keep_proportion` on, so it fits **within** the box and keeps the aspect - 1528x2736 -> 474x848, 2048x1024 -> 480x240, so landscape footage is not cropped. Raise `width`/`height` (or turn `keep_proportion` off, or remove the node) for full-size joints and a full-size render preview.

**Traps:**

* The smoother applies to the **exported file**, not the preview. `SAM3DBody_Render` reads the pose data
  directly, so the render stays as jittery as the raw prediction - judge the GLB, not the overlay.
* `Save3DAdvanced` needs the 3D viewport, so a headless run must pass `viewport_state: {}` and explicit
  width/height (the frontend writes a widget slot for that socket, which shifts them by one).
* **Gate the result:** `scripts/motion_quality.py <file.glb>` reports jitter and single-frame breaks. Zero
  breaks is the bar, and no smoothing setting cleared every clip we tested.
* `camera_translation` is `off` here, so the root stays at its bind position and the render does not sit on
  the performer; `centered`/`absolute` bake the camera translation into the root instead.

**Subject selection (the per-clip decisions):**
- The `conditioning` on `SAM3_VideoTrack` (and the `class_name` on the RT-DETR boxes) selects *what to track* - they have no effect on the mesh's appearance. `person` is the minimal correct prompt for a single-subject clip; multi-person clips need a distinguishing phrase plus the boxes. `class_name` is a **closed COCO-class dropdown** - set it to the subject's category (zebra, car, ...); a subject outside the class list means skipping the boxes and leaning on the prompt or an initial mask.
- **`initial_mask`** is the third way to select the subject: a mask on the first frame tracks that region without any text prompt (the node requires one of the two).
- **`BuildPoseFile.track_index`** picks which tracked person is exported: **-1 = all tracks** (each gets its own motion), >= 0 = a single track. With one person in frame, leave it.

**Input:** this ships pointing at the upstream example clip, `input/woman_holding_water_glass.mp4` (from the
Comfy-Org `workflow_templates` repo) - upload it, or point `LoadVideo` at your own footage.

*How to run it: story **S17** in `HOWTO.md`  ·  Why it is this way: **E4/E6/E8/E15/E16** in `animation/EXPERIMENTS.md`.*

Derived from the upstream ComfyUI template `utility_sam3d_body.json`, with the two values above changed and
this note replaced; the graph is otherwise upstream's.

**The export style decides whether the face exists at all.** `BuildPoseFile` ships `mesh_style = body_mesh`, so the MHR body mesh (18,439 verts) is written and the **72 facial blendshapes are attached to it as morph targets** - that is what makes the exported clip carry a face. The other option, `scail`, exports a stick figure: ~25x smaller (728 KB against 18 MB) and the same skeleton, but with no body mesh, so **the face is dropped silently** (it was, until E20). The face knobs are on `SAM3DBody_FaceExpression`: `strength`, `mouth_strength`, `eye_strength`, `brow_strength` and `blendshape_smooth_window`; the morph targets are unnamed, so a rig's face maps onto them by index. The shapes are **unnamed in the GLB**, but the exporter emits them in basis order, so target `k` is MHR axis `k` - `face-shapes.md` names the 44 that video can drive. `fps` is wired from the clip (a 30 fps source used to export 25% slow).

**Upstream template notes (merged from stray note nodes):**
- MoGe can be optionally used to detect FoV for more accurate alignment with source video.
- For multiple people in same clip SAM3 is practically required, otherwise optional but can improve detection
- While bounding boxes are technically optional, depending on clip will improve detection accuracy drastically.
- Sam3d-body does not detect face expressions, this node adds them through MediaPipe face detection.
